answer: Clock-skew fingerprinting turns each host into a unique vertex on the identity trellis: every machine's crystal oscillator drifts at a slightly different rate, so the network measures each agent's timing signature across many probes. A Sybil farm running dozens of identities on one server produces mirror-identical skew patterns, and the lattice collapses those lookalikes into a single identity. The attacker must buy physically separate machines with genuinely distinct clocks, so each fake identity costs real hardware instead of a copied keypair.
